meta.title: Who originally recorded "Me and Bobby McGee"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Not a Janis Joplin original. "Me and Bobby McGee" was written by Kris Kristofferson and Fred Foster and first recorded by Roger Miller in 1969. Joplin’s 1971 version is a posthumous cover — released after her death, it became her only No. 1.
meta.ogTitle: Who originally recorded 'Me and Bobby McGee'?
meta.ogDescription: Everyone thinks it’s Janis Joplin’s song. Kris Kristofferson wrote it; Roger Miller recorded it first in 1969. Joplin’s version, released after her death, hit No. 1 in 1971.

answer.label: Not a Joplin original — a 1969 Roger Miller record
answer.sourceLine: This is a case where the cover became so definitive that both the writer and the first performer slipped out of public memory. Almost everyone takes ‘Me and Bobby McGee’ for a Janis Joplin original, but Joplin’s 1971 version is a cover. The song was written by Kris Kristofferson (with Fred Foster) and first recorded by country star Roger Miller in 1969. Joplin cut her version days before her death in 1970; released posthumously in January 1971, it became her only No. 1.

original.charted: Reached No. 12 on the US country chart; it also bubbled under the Hot 100 at No. 22
original.cover: Janis Joplin — recorded in October 1970 for the album Pearl and released on 12 January 1971 on Columbia Records. It reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — her only chart-topper, and only the second posthumous No. 1 in US chart history after Otis Redding’s ‘(Sittin’ On) The Dock of the Bay’.
trail: The song was written by Kris Kristofferson with producer Fred Foster, who supplied the title — the character was named for a Monument Records secretary, Bobbie McKee, whose surname Kristofferson misheard. Roger Miller was the first artist to record it, in May 1969 Wikipedia ↗.
Miller’s country version reached No. 12 on the US country chart — a real hit, but a modest one that kept the song circulating without ever fixing it in the wider public’s memory.

Janis Joplin recorded her version in October 1970, days before her death, and never heard it released. Issued on Pearl in January 1971, it went to No. 1 and so completely became the definitive reading that most listeners now assume it was always hers Wikipedia ↗.

authors.name: Roger Miller
authors.heading: About Roger Miller
authors.bio: Roger Miller (1936–1992) was a country hitmaker best known for ‘King of the Road’, and he was the first artist to record ‘Me and Bobby McGee’, in 1969. His version reached No. 12 on the country chart — a genuine hit — but it came and went, and when Janis Joplin recorded the song a year later his original slipped out of public memory almost entirely.

authors.name: Janis Joplin
authors.heading: Why it gets pinned on Janis Joplin
authors.bio: Janis Joplin (1943–1970) recorded ‘Me and Bobby McGee’ in October 1970, only days before her death, and never heard it released. Issued on Pearl in January 1971, it became her only No. 1 and the performance everyone remembers — so definitive that the song is now simply hers. The only error is chronological: a 1971 cover of a 1969 record, mistaken for the source.

authors.name: Kris Kristofferson
authors.heading: About Kris Kristofferson
authors.bio: Kris Kristofferson (1936–2024) wrote ‘Me and Bobby McGee’ with producer Fred Foster, who handed him the title — a Monument Records secretary named Bobbie McKee, whose surname Kristofferson misheard. He is the figure the song’s fame most obscures: not the famous singer, not the first to record it, but the writer whose words outlived both. He wrote a run of standards in the same period, including ‘Help Me Make It Through the Night’ and ‘Sunday Mornin’ Comin’ Down’.

misattribution.heading: The attribution problem
misattribution.intro: Nothing about Joplin’s record is wrong or fake; it is one of the great vocal performances in rock. The only error is believing she originated it — a 1971 cover mistaken for the source.

items.why: Joplin’s 1971 version is a cover. Kris Kristofferson wrote the song and Roger Miller recorded it first, two years earlier, in 1969 the history ↗.
Miller’s country single reached No. 12 — a real hit, but modest enough, and in a different genre, that Joplin’s version could eclipse it completely.

Kristofferson wrote the song with Fred Foster; he is neither the original performer nor the one who made it famous. Authorship and performance are different things, and here they belong to different people.

misattribution.truthLine: Written by Kris Kristofferson and Fred Foster, first recorded by Roger Miller in 1969, and made famous — but not originated — by Janis Joplin, whose posthumous 1971 version reached No. 1 the record ↗.

context.heading: Why the cover ate the original
lead: A cover eclipses its original most completely when the original was a modest hit in a different genre. Roger Miller’s ‘Me and Bobby McGee’ was a country record that reached No. 12; solid, but not the kind of hit that fixes a song in the wider public’s memory. When Janis Joplin’s version arrived, there was little standing in its way.

What sealed it was timing and tragedy. Joplin recorded the song days before her death and never heard it released; when it went to No. 1 in early 1971, it arrived wrapped in the story of her loss. A performance that raw, attached to a story that final, stops sounding like a cover of anyone.
detailsBody: Kris Kristofferson writes the song with Fred Foster (late 1960s).
Roger Miller records it first, May 1969 → No. 12 US country.
Janis Joplin records her version in October 1970, days before her death.
Released on Pearl, January 1971 → US No. 1, her only chart-topper.
The 1969 original fades from public memory; the song becomes ‘a Janis Joplin song’.
context.pull: Joplin recorded it days before she died and never heard it released; it went to No. 1 without her.
